fact_sheet.business_description: The Company is a supplier of automotive components and systems currently operating in Chapter 11 bankruptcy [D01]. It maintains a manufacturing footprint and engineering relationships that may hold going-concern value, though its capital structure is impaired [D01, D06].

final.memo:
The Company is currently operating in Chapter 11 bankruptcy, representing a distressed credit opportunity where the market has conflated temporary liquidity constraints with terminal impairment [D01, D03]. While the common equity is effectively wiped out by the staggering $14,011m book equity deficit, we see distinct value in the senior credit stack [D02, D04]. The market is paralyzed by the Q1 2009 revenue decline and the immediate cash burn, ignoring the underlying worth of the company’s manufacturing and engineering relationships [D01, D03, D06].

Our recovery analysis focuses on the $541m in first-priority senior claims, specifically Tranches A and B [D04]. We believe the going-concern value of these assets will be protected during the court-supervised reorganization, providing a hard floor for our position that is significantly higher than the current distressed pricing [D01, D06]. By stepping into these senior tranches, we gain a seat at the table during the most critical phase of the restructuring [D04].

The immediate catalyst is the final financing hearing scheduled for June 16, 2009 [D03, D07]. Our primary ask is the court's approval of the proposed subordinated DIP financing, which is the key to maintaining entity integrity [D03, D07]. Should the court or creditors move to undermine these specific senior tranches, we are prepared to organize a creditor committee to challenge the plan and enforce our seniority [D03, D04]. 

We are sizing this position at 3% of NAV, which is appropriate for a high-conviction distressed credit play [D04, D05]. We intend to hedge the sector-specific volatility and broader automotive correlation by utilizing index puts or credit default swaps [D05]. Our exit strategy is tied to the successful confirmation of a reorganization plan that validates our recovery thesis, allowing us to capture the upside as the capital structure stabilizes [D03, D07].
